text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.2% today as oil prices bounced back after a five-day losing streak, with diplomatic hopes for the Middle East providing some relief. News that Iran floated conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine signaled openness to an energy ceasefire with Russia reduced the geopolitical premium that had been weighing on crude. Brent crude (the world benchmark) sits at $130.80 per barrel, still elevated, which supports refiner and producer margins.

The stock's 6% decline over the past two weeks reflects real concern about potential supply disruptions and geopolitical tension easing — lower prices for oil hurt producers like ConocoPhillips. Today's move is a modest rebound on tentative peace signals rather than a reversal of that downward trend; the company still faces headwinds if diplomatic progress continues and removes the risk premium from crude.
